answer: Each identity must hold a private shard of a public data canyon. The network audits it with a sonnet of fourteen random retrieval checks. The agent must return the requested bytes and a quartz-clear hash proof within the deadline. A sybil must rent storage and bandwidth for every key, so k fake identities cost k times the disk and traffic, and sharing one store creates correlated access times that expose the cluster. Honest agents pay for one shard. Attackers pay per voice and risk losing the whole cluster in one audit.
